ordered_diagnoses: ewing sarcoma of the external ear canal

s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
MRI showed a 5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid
Lesion had heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
Expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve
Erosion of the posterior external auditory canal
Expansion of the stylomastoid foramen

raw.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal

differentials: ewing sarcoma of the external ear canal

shortlist: ewing sarcoma of the external ear canal

raw.rationale: The patient's gradual-onset right facial weakness, nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal, and imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid with heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast and expansion of the fallopian canal are consistent with a vestibular schwannoma.

rejected.label: facial palsy
rejected.why: Facial palsy is a symptom, not a diagnosis, and does not explain the mass or imaging findings.

rejected.label: acoustic neuroma
rejected.why: Acoustic neuroma is another term for vestibular schwannoma, but it is not a distinct entity in this case.

rejected.label: ewing sarcoma of the external ear canal
rejected.why: Ewing sarcoma is a malignant tumor that would likely present with more aggressive symptoms and imaging findings.

rejected.label: hearing impairment
rejected.why: Hearing impairment is a symptom, and the patient's mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz is not the primary diagnosis.
